newsitem.title: GERMANY: German firms aim to check logistics costs.
newsitem.headline: German firms aim to check logistics costs.

text.p: Large German companies aim over the coming few years to keep the share of total costs spent on logistics at current levels despite the trend towards global production, a leading transport expert told a German freight managers congress.

Professor Helmut Baumgarten said Germany industry has cut transport and distribution costs to 11.3 percent of total costs in recent years from 15 percent years and expected to maintain this ratio up to 2000 despite rising logistics costs generated by globalisation.

Trading companies have cut logistics costs to 21 percent of total costs from 23 percent and were aiming to reduce this to 18 percent, he told a news conference of the German Logistics Association (BVL) at its annual German Logistics Congress in Berlin.

Baumgarten said a BVL and Berlin Technical University survey of 650 firms showed 70 percent accepted that a logistics strategy for Germany alone was insufficient to ensure long-term economic survival.
More than 50 percent of large companies already had global logistics concepts, while nearly a third of medium-sized firms planned worldwide logistics schemes, the survey showed.
Global logistics concepts could offer integrated, rapid and optimal transport services combining air, sea, road and rail transport, Baumgarten said.
"Transport suppliers such as Deutsche Bahn have produced regardless of the customer for years. Logistics shippers are clients who want efficient, functioning networks," he said.
Corporate freight managers were ready to increase rail transport shipments 50 percent over the next five years but Deutsche Bahn was not able to offer client-orientated transport services, he stated.

Globalisation of production was being led by the semiconductor and computer industries, followed rapidly by the automobile industry, which all required logistics services to ensure delivery and distribution, he added.

Companies would in future require less than 50 percent of parts and materials to be delivered from Germany, with growing shares from North America, East Asia and Eastern Europe, the Berlin University survey showed.

Companies also recognised the need for electronic communications networks, faster delivery processes through integrated transport and the chance to outsource their logistics requirements, Baumgarten said.
Electronic data interchange (EDI) had tripled in recent years but was still insufficiently used, particularly by smaller companies, he added.

BVL chairman Hanspeter Stabenau said the record number of 1,400 participants from 14 countries, including a Chinese delegation, at the "Global Tendency" congress showed the growing recognition of logistics as a central part of corporate operations.

Some 350 attendees were company managers or directors. Most participants came from service, transport, industry and computer sectors, he said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
